Shri Vipin Sanghi, C.J.
Shri Ramesh Chandra Khulbe, J.
Ms. Neeti Rana, learned counsel holding 
brief of Mr. Pankaj Chaturvedi, learned 
counsel for the appellant.
Mr. B.S. Parihar, learned Standing 
Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned counsel for 
respondent nos.2 and 3.
Mr. Prashant Khanna, learned counsel
for respondent no.4.
Learned counsel for the appellant is out 
of station. Adjournment is sought.
At her request, adjourned to 
09.01.2023.
Counter-affidavit filed by the 
respondent nos.2 and 3 as well as counter￾affidavit filed by respondent no.4 are taken 
on record.
We find that the respondents have
moved the application to seek direction for 
taking the counter-affidavit on record.
In our view, such an application is not 
necessary to be filed as there is nothing to 
show that the counter affidavit has been 
filed belatedly. Only when the counter 
affidavit is filed beyond the time granted by 
the Court it would be necessary for the 
respondent to move an application to seek 
condonation of delay.
The petitioner may file the rejoinder 
within four weeks.
List on 09.01.2023.
(R.C. Khulbe, J.) (Vipin Sanghi, C.J.)

Adjournment is sought on behalf of 
counsel for the appellant. 
Mr. Bahuguna, learned Senior Counsel 
opposes the same on the ground that the 
appellant is unnecessarily delaying the 
matter. 
As a last and final opportunity, 
adjourned to 20.06.2023. 
It is made clear that no further 
adjourned shall be granted. 
We make it clear that the order granting stay of the judgment dated 01.12.2021, 
passed in Writ Petition (S/S) No. 576 of 
2018, does not come in the way of 
respondent authority in proceeding to act in 
terms of the selection made without 
prejudice to the rights and contentions of the 
parties.
